# Calculate dynamic time windows
START_TIME=$(date -u -d "30 days ago" +%FT%TZ)
END_TIME=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)

# Print a well-organized table header
printf "%-25s %-25s %-12s %-12s\n" "INSTANCE ID" "TIMESTAMP" "AVERAGE (%)" "MAXIMUM (%)"
printf "%s\n" "----------------------------------------------------------------------------------"

# Iterate through every instance ID
for INSTANCE_ID in "${INSTANCE_IDS[@]}"; do

    # Execute the AWS CloudWatch command using the requested text output format
    # We use a precise client-side query path to isolate just the Timestamp, Average, and Maximum values
    aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics \
        --namespace AWS/EC2 \
        --metric-name CPUUtilization \
        --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value="${INSTANCE_ID}" \
        --statistics Average Maximum \
        --start-time "${START_TIME}" \
        --end-time "${END_TIME}" \
donedone    fi  printf "%-25s %-25s %-12s %-12s\n" "${INSTANCE_ID}" "${TIMESTAMP}" "${FORMATTED_AVG}" "${FORMATTED_MAX}"
